translations.literal: There was also the Zhandui native official beyond Dajianlu, amid ten thousand mountains, who relied on the terrain to plunder brazenly, raiding as far as relay-station troops; the local officials captured and punished them.
translations.idiomatic: There was also the Zhandui chieftain beyond Dajianlu, deep in the mountains, who used the terrain to raid boldly, even attacking relay-station troops, until local officials captured and punished the offenders.

sentences.zh: 上瞻對土目四朗、下瞻對土目班滾匿罪人不出。

translations.literal: The upper Zhandui native chief Silang and the lower Zhandui native chief Ban Bong harbored criminals and refused to surrender them.
translations.idiomatic: The upper Zhandui chieftain Silang and the lower Zhandui chieftain Ban Bong sheltered fugitives and refused to hand them over.

sentences.zh: 十年，慶復偕巡撫紀山、提督李質粹疏請發兵進剿，上命宜妥協周詳，毋少疏忽。

translations.literal: In the tenth year Qing Fu, together with Provincial Governor Ji Shan and Brigade Commander Li Zhicui, memorialized asking to send troops to advance and suppress them; the emperor ordered that matters be handled with compromise, thoroughness, and no slight negligence.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year Qing Fu, together with Governor Ji Shan and Brigade Commander Li Zhicui, memorialized for a punitive expedition. The emperor ordered that the campaign be conducted with care, thorough planning, and no negligence.

sentences.zh: 慶復遂發兵，質粹進駐東俄洛，扼兩瞻對總隘；

translations.literal: Qing Fu then sent troops; Zhicui advanced and stationed at Dong'e Luo, holding the main passes of upper and lower Zhandui;
translations.idiomatic: Qing Fu then mobilized. Zhicui advanced to Dong'e Luo and seized the main passes between upper and lower Zhandui;

sentences.zh: 夔州副將馬良柱出里塘為南路，松潘總兵宋宗璋出甘孜為北路，建昌總兵袁士弼出沙晉隆為中路，刻期並發，四朗詣宗璋軍降。

translations.literal: Kui Prefecture Vice Commander Ma Liangzhu came out from Litang as the southern route, Songpan Commander Song Zongzhang came out from Ganzi as the northern route, and Jianchang Commander Yuan Shibi came out from Shajinlong as the central route; on a set date all launched together, and Silang came to Zongzhang's army and surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Kui Prefecture vice commander Ma Liangzhu marched from Litang on the southern route, Songpan commander Song Zongzhang from Ganzi on the north, and Jianchang commander Yuan Shibi from Shajinlong in the center. On the appointed day all columns moved together, and Silang surrendered to Song Zongzhang.

sentences.zh: 士弼自擴城頂趨納爾格，與番人戰加社袨卡諸地，屢勝。

translations.literal: Shibi from Kuochengding pressed toward Na'erge and fought the tribesmen at Jiasheka and other places, winning repeatedly.
translations.idiomatic: Shibi pushed from Kuochengding toward Na'erge and fought the tribes at Jiasheka and elsewhere, winning battle after battle.

sentences.zh: 良柱攻嚓嗎所，焚其寨三，地雷發，番人死甚眾。

translations.literal: Liangzhu attacked Chamahuo, burned three of its stockades, land mines erupted, and very many tribesmen died.
translations.idiomatic: Liangzhu assaulted Chamahuo, burned three stockades, and set off land mines that killed a great many tribesmen.

sentences.zh: 上下瞻對夾江而居，四朗居江西地，曰撒墩，其從子肯硃居江東地，曰孺耳，班滾亦居江西地，曰如郎。

translations.literal: Upper and lower Zhandui lay on either side of the river; Silang dwelt on the west bank in a place called Sadun, his nephew Kenzhu dwelt on the east bank in a place called Ru'er, and Ban Bong also dwelt on the west bank in a place called Rulang.
translations.idiomatic: Upper and lower Zhandui straddled the river. Silang held the west bank at Sadun; his nephew Kenzhu held the east at Ru'er; Ban Bong also held the west bank at Rulang.

sentences.zh: 江東木魯工為要隘。

translations.literal: Mulugong on the east bank was a strategic pass.
translations.idiomatic: Mulugong on the east bank was the key choke point.

sentences.zh: 四朗既降，宗璋兵越撒墩駐阿賽，去如郎數十里，良柱亦逼進如郎，質粹發兵往應，班滾力拒。

translations.literal: Silang having surrendered, Zongzhang's troops crossed Sadun and stationed at Asai, several tens of li from Rulang; Liangzhu also pressed forward toward Rulang, Zhicui dispatched troops to support him, and Ban Bong resisted fiercely.
translations.idiomatic: After Silang surrendered, Song Zongzhang crossed Sadun and encamped at Asai, a few dozen li from Rulang. Liangzhu pressed toward Rulang as well, Zhicui sent reinforcements, and Ban Bong resisted stubbornly.

sentences.zh: 宗璋分兵自然多會士弼，克臘蓋，破底硃。

translations.literal: Zongzhang divided his troops and joined Shibi at Ziranduo, captured Lagai, and broke Dizhu.
translations.idiomatic: Song Zongzhang detached a column to join Shibi at Ziranduo, took Lagai, and stormed Dizhu.

sentences.zh: 良柱亦撫定番寨四十六。

translations.literal: Liangzhu also pacified forty-six tribal stockades.
translations.idiomatic: Liangzhu also brought forty-six tribal stockades to submission.

sentences.zh: 班滾請降，慶復不許。

translations.literal: Ban Bong asked to surrender; Qing Fu did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: Ban Bong offered to surrender, but Qing Fu refused.

sentences.zh: 疏入，上命毋恃勝輕敵。

translations.literal: When the memorial arrived, the emperor ordered that they not rely on victory and slight the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: When the report arrived, the emperor warned them not to grow overconfident after their victories.

sentences.zh: 尋授慶復文華殿大學士，仍留總督。

translations.literal: Soon Qing Fu was appointed Grand Secretary of the Wenhua Hall while still retaining the governorship.
translations.idiomatic: Qing Fu was soon made a Grand Secretary of the Wenhua Hall while remaining governor-general.

sentences.zh: 十一年春，慶復進駐東俄洛，奏言：「前克底硃，班滾母率頭人至軍前請降，質粹遣令歸。

translations.literal: In the spring of the eleventh year Qing Fu advanced and stationed at Dong'e Luo, memorializing: "When we previously captured Dizhu, Ban Bong's mother led headmen to the army front to request surrender, and Zhicui dispatched them to return.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the eleventh year Qing Fu moved forward to Dong'e Luo and reported: "After we took Dizhu, Ban Bong's mother came to camp with headmen to sue for peace, and Zhicui sent them back.

sentences.zh: 臣諮詢質粹，令速進兵。」

translations.literal: Your servant consulted Zhicui and ordered him to advance troops speedily."
translations.idiomatic: I questioned Zhicui and ordered him to press the attack at once."

sentences.zh: 上責質粹失機，慶復又疏劾士弼意主招降，請奪官，仍戴罪效力。

translations.literal: The emperor reproved Zhicui for missing the opportunity; Qing Fu again memorialized impeaching Shibi for intending chiefly to accept surrender, asking that his office be stripped while he still wore guilt to render merit.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor rebuked Zhicui for letting the moment slip. Qing Fu also impeached Shibi for favoring negotiation over pursuit, asked that his rank be stripped, and allowed him to continue serving under sentence of guilt.

sentences.zh: 尋自東俄洛進駐靈雀，以明正土司汪結及降人騷達邦、俄木丁等為導，自茹色以皮船渡，破十餘卡，逼如郎，攻泥日寨，圍之數日，焚碉。

translations.literal: Soon from Dong'e Luo he advanced and stationed at Lingque, using the Mingzheng native official Wang Jie and the surrendered men Saodabang, Emuding, and others as guides; from Ruse he crossed by leather boat, broke more than ten passes, pressed Rulang, attacked the Nirizai stockade, besieged it for several days, and burned the watchtowers.
translations.idiomatic: He soon advanced from Dong'e Luo to Lingque, guided by the Mingzheng chieftain Wang Jie and defectors including Saodabang and Emuding. Crossing at Ruse in skin boats, he stormed more than ten blockhouses, closed on Rulang, and besieged the Nirizai stockade for days before burning its towers.

sentences.zh: 質粹諮慶復，言班滾已焚死，又言焚碉時，火光中望見番酋懸縊。

translations.literal: Zhicui consulted Qing Fu, saying Ban Bong had already been burned to death, and also saying that when the watchtowers were burned, in the firelight he glimpsed the tribal chieftain hanging himself.
translations.idiomatic: Zhicui informed Qing Fu that Ban Bong had died in the fire, and claimed that amid the flames he had seen the chieftain hanging himself.

sentences.zh: 慶復詢於眾，俄木丁於燼中得鳥槍銅捥，謂班滾物也，遂以班滾焚斃疏聞。

translations.literal: Qing Fu inquired among the crowd; Emuding obtained a musket's copper socket from the embers and said it was Ban Bong's object; he then memorialized that Ban Bong had been burned to death.
translations.idiomatic: Qing Fu questioned those present. Emuding pulled a musket socket from the ashes and declared it Ban Bong's. On this basis Qing Fu reported that Ban Bong had perished in the flames.

sentences.zh: 上察慶復師逼如郎時，嘗奏班滾走沙加邦河，土目姜錯太迎入寨，未言至泥日；

translations.literal: The emperor examined that when Qing Fu's army pressed Rulang, he had once memorialized that Ban Bong fled to the Shajiabang River and the native chief Jiang Cuotai welcomed him into a stockade, but had not said he reached Niriz;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor noted that when Qing Fu's army closed on Rulang, he had reported Ban Bong fleeing to the Shajiabang River and being sheltered by the native officer Jiang Cuotai, without mentioning Nirizai;

sentences.zh: 諭慶復，班滾渠魁斷不可漏網，毋留遺孽，毋墮狡計。

translations.literal: he instructed Qing Fu that the ringleader Ban Bong absolutely could not escape the net, that no remnant evils should be left, and that they must not fall into a cunning stratagem.
translations.idiomatic: and instructed Qing Fu that the ringleader Ban Bong must not slip through the net, that no remnant faction be left alive, and that they must not be taken in by deception.

sentences.zh: 尋加慶復太子太保。

translations.literal: Soon Qing Fu was additionally made Crown Prince Grand Guardian.
translations.idiomatic: Qing Fu was soon made Crown Prince Grand Guardian as well.

sentences.zh: 慶復又劾士弼怯懦乖張，奪官，逮下刑部論罪。

translations.literal: Qing Fu again impeached Shibi as cowardly and perverse, stripped his office, and had him arrested and sent down to the Ministry of Punishments for sentencing.
translations.idiomatic: Qing Fu impeached Shibi again for cowardice and insubordination, stripped his rank, and had him sent to the Ministry of Punishments for trial.

sentences.zh: 十二年，大金川土酋莎羅奔為亂，上授張廣泗川陝總督，召慶復入閣治事，命兼管兵部。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year the Greater Jinchuan native chief Suoluoben rebelled; the emperor appointed Zhang Guangsi Sichuan-Shaanxi Governor-General, summoned Qing Fu into the Grand Council to handle affairs, and ordered him additionally to manage the Board of War.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year the Greater Jinchuan chieftain Suoluoben rose in rebellion. The emperor appointed Zhang Guangsi governor-general of Sichuan and Shaanxi, recalled Qing Fu to the Grand Council, and put him in charge of the Board of War as well.

sentences.zh: 尋廣泗奏言訊土司汪結，言班滾尚匿如郎未死，慶復得班滾子沙加七立，為更名德昌喇嘛，令仍居班滾大碉，冒稱經堂。

translations.literal: Soon Guangsi memorialized that on interrogating the native official Wang Jie, he said Ban Bong still hid at Rulang and was not dead; Qing Fu had obtained Ban Bong's son Shajia Qili, renamed him Dechang Lama, ordered him still to dwell in Ban Bong's great watchtower, and falsely called it a scripture hall.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Guangsi soon reported that under interrogation the chieftain Wang Jie said Ban Bong was still alive and hiding at Rulang. Qing Fu had taken Ban Bong's son Shajia Qili, renamed him Dechang Lama, installed him in Ban Bong's great tower, and passed it off as a chapel.

sentences.zh: 上責慶復欺罔，奪官待罪。

translations.literal: The emperor reproved Qing Fu for deception, stripped his office, and left him awaiting punishment.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor condemned Qing Fu for deceit, stripped his offices, and left him to await sentence.

sentences.zh: 欽差大臣尚書班第奏言師克如郎，班滾已逃，僅得空寨。

translations.literal: The Imperial Commissioner, Minister Ban Di, memorialized that the army captured Rulang, Ban Bong had already fled, and they obtained only an empty stockade.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial commissioner Ban Di reported that the army took Rulang but Ban Bong had already escaped, leaving only empty stockades.

sentences.zh: 上逮質粹下刑部獄，召宗璋與質。

translations.literal: The emperor had Zhicui arrested and sent down to the Ministry of Punishments prison, and summoned Zongzhang to confront and question him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had Zhicui imprisoned in the Ministry of Punishments and summoned Song Zongzhang to confront him.

sentences.zh: 質粹言：「曩報班滾焚斃，實未親見；

translations.literal: Zhicui said: "When I formerly reported that Ban Bong was burned to death, I had not actually seen it myself;
translations.idiomatic: Zhicui said: "When I reported that Ban Bong had burned to death, I had not seen it with my own eyes;

sentences.zh: 後聞藏匿山洞，亦未告慶復追捕。」

translations.literal: later I heard he was hiding in a mountain cave, but I also did not inform Qing Fu to pursue and capture him."
translations.idiomatic: later I heard he was hiding in a cave, but I never told Qing Fu to hunt him down."

sentences.zh: 上命下慶復刑部獄，令軍機大臣會訊，按律定擬，坐貽誤軍機律論斬。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered Qing Fu sent down to the Ministry of Punishments prison, commanded the Grand Council ministers to conduct a joint interrogation, fixed the sentence according to law, and convicted him under the statute on delaying military affairs, sentencing him to decapitation.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had Qing Fu imprisoned as well, ordered the Grand Council to try him jointly, and under the statute on dereliction in military affairs sentenced him to death.

sentences.zh: 十四年九月，賜自盡。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the fourteenth year he was granted permission to take his own life.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of the fourteenth year he was granted suicide in lieu of execution.

sentences.zh: 李質粹，漢軍正白旗人。

translations.literal: Li Zhicui was a man of the Hanjun Plain White Banner.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zhicui was a member of the Hanjun Plain White Banner.

sentences.zh: 雍正初，自把總擢藍翎侍衛。

translations.literal: In the early Yongzheng period he was promoted from corporal to Blue Plume Bodyguard.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Yongzheng reign he rose from corporal to Blue Plume Bodyguard.

sentences.zh: 嘗從年羹堯出師，累擢陝西、固原提督。

translations.literal: He once followed Nian Gengyao on campaign and was repeatedly promoted to Brigade Commander of Shaanxi and Guyuan.
translations.idiomatic: He campaigned under Nian Gengyao and was eventually promoted to brigade commander of Shaanxi and Guyuan.

sentences.zh: 丁憂，命署四川提督。

translations.literal: While in mourning leave he was ordered to act as Sichuan Brigade Commander.
translations.idiomatic: During a period of mourning he was appointed acting brigade commander of Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 附和慶復妄言班滾死，慶復死之明年，斬質粹。

translations.literal: He echoed Qing Fu's false report that Ban Bong was dead; the year after Qing Fu died, Zhicui was executed by decapitation.
translations.idiomatic: He echoed Qing Fu's false claim that Ban Bong was dead. The year after Qing Fu's death, Zhicui was beheaded.

sentences.zh: 張廣泗，漢軍鑲紅旗人。

translations.literal: Zhang Guangsi was a man of the Hanjun Bordered Red Banner.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Guangsi was a member of the Hanjun Bordered Red Banner.

sentences.zh: 以監生入貲授知府。

translations.literal: As a student entering through donation he was granted the post of prefect.
translations.idiomatic: He purchased office as a student and was appointed prefect.

sentences.zh: 康熙六十一年，選貴州思州。

translations.literal: In the sixty-first year of Kangxi he was selected for Guizhou's Sizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixty-first year of the Kangxi reign he was assigned to Sizhou in Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 雍正四年，調雲南楚雄。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Yongzheng he was transferred to Chuxiong in Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Yongzheng he was transferred to Chuxiong in Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 雲貴總督鄂爾泰討亂苗，以廣泗佐其事，奏改調黎平。

translations.literal: Yunnan-Guizhou Governor-General Ortai campaigned against rebellious Miao and used Guangsi to assist the matter; he memorialized to transfer him to Liping.
translations.idiomatic: When Yunnan-Guizhou governor-general Ortai campaigned against rebellious Miao, Guangsi assisted him and was transferred to Liping on Ortai's recommendation.

sentences.zh: 五年，擢貴州按察使。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was promoted to Guizhou Surveillance Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he was promoted to surveillance commissioner of Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 六年，廣泗率兵赴都勻、黎平、鎮遠、清平諸地化導群苗，相機剿撫，超授巡撫。

translations.literal: In the sixth year Guangsi led troops to Duyun, Liping, Zhenyuan, Qingping, and other places to transform and guide the various Miao, suppressing or pacifying as circumstances required, and was specially promoted to Provincial Governor.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year Guangsi led troops through Duyun, Liping, Zhenyuan, Qingping, and neighboring districts to win over the Miao tribes, campaigning or negotiating as circumstances required, and was promoted straight to provincial governor.

sentences.zh: 清平屬丹江苗最悍，廣泗遣兵分道攻克小丹江、大丹江及雞溝等寨。

translations.literal: Under Qingping the Danjiang Miao were fiercest; Guangsi dispatched troops by separate routes and captured the stockades of Xiao Danjiang, Da Danjiang, Jigou, and others.
translations.idiomatic: The Danjiang Miao under Qingping were the fiercest. Guangsi sent columns by separate routes and took the stockades of Xiao Danjiang, Da Danjiang, Jigou, and others.

sentences.zh: 鎮遠屬上九股諸寨與接壤，亦次第降。

translations.literal: The various stockades of Shang Jiugu under Zhenyuan, bordering them, also surrendered in sequence.
translations.idiomatic: The Shang Jiugu stockades on the Zhenyuan border also submitted one after another.

sentences.zh: 下九股、清水江、古州諸苗悉定。

translations.literal: The Miao of Xia Jiugu, the Qingshui River, and Guzhou were all pacified.
translations.idiomatic: The Miao of Xia Jiugu, the Qingshui River, and Guzhou were all brought to order.

sentences.zh: 疏聞，上命與鄂爾泰詳議善後諸事，語詳鄂爾泰傳。

translations.literal: When the memorial was reported, the emperor ordered that he and Ortai deliberate in detail on matters of good governance afterward; the account is detailed in Ortai's biography.
translations.idiomatic: When his report arrived, the emperor ordered him and Ortai to work out the post-pacification arrangements in detail, as recounted in Ortai's biography.

sentences.zh: 十年，廣泗疏言：「清水江及都江為黔、楚、粵三省通流，當設哨船聯絡聲勢。

translations.literal: In the tenth year Guangsi memorialized: "The Qingshui River and the Dujiang are common waterways of Guizhou, Chu, and Yue; sentinel boats should be established to link their strength in coordination.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year Guangsi wrote: "The Qingshui River and the Dujiang are shared waterways of Guizhou, Huguang, and Guangdong. Patrol boats should be posted to keep the regions in communication.

sentences.zh: 古州應貯米，責成同知以下董理。

translations.literal: Guzhou should store grain, charging the subprefect and officials below to supervise management.
translations.idiomatic: Guzhou should maintain grain reserves, with the subprefect and lower officials responsible for oversight.

sentences.zh: 譯人分別勤惰予糈，並授土官劄付，宣布條約，化導苗民。」

translations.literal: Interpreters were to distinguish diligence and laziness in granting grain rations, and native officials were to be granted patents, treaties proclaimed, and Miao people transformed and guided."
translations.idiomatic: Interpreters should be paid according to diligence, native officers granted patents of appointment, treaties proclaimed, and the Miao brought under civil guidance."

sentences.zh: 下部議行。

translations.literal: It was sent to the ministry for deliberation and implementation.
translations.idiomatic: The proposals were sent to the relevant ministry for approval and implementation.

sentences.zh: 敘功，授拜他喇布勒哈番世職。

translations.literal: His merit was narrated and he was granted the hereditary office of baturu rank.
translations.idiomatic: For his services he was granted the hereditary rank of baturu.

sentences.zh: 準噶爾擾邊，寧遠大將軍岳鍾琪率師出西路。

translations.literal: The Zungars disturbed the border; Ningyuan Grand General Yue Zhongqi led an army out on the western route.
translations.idiomatic: When the Zungars raided the frontier, Ningyuan grand general Yue Zhongqi led an army westward.

sentences.zh: 上授廣泗副將軍，召詣京師授方略。

translations.literal: The emperor appointed Guangsi Deputy General, summoned him to the capital, and granted him strategy.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor made Guangsi deputy commander, summoned him to the capital, and briefed him on strategy.

sentences.zh: 廣泗至軍，鍾琪方自巴爾廣爾移軍穆壘。

translations.literal: When Guangsi reached the army, Zhongqi had just moved his troops from Barkul to Mulei.
translations.idiomatic: Guangsi reached the front just as Zhongqi was moving his force from Barkul to Mulei.

sentences.zh: 廣泗將四千人出鄂隆吉，與鍾琪會於科舍圖，至穆壘。

translations.literal: Guangsi led four thousand men out from Elongji, joined Zhongqi at Keshetu, and arrived at Mulei.
translations.idiomatic: Guangsi marched four thousand men from Elongji, joined Zhongqi at Keshetu, and advanced to Mulei.

sentences.zh: 上召鍾琪還京師，命廣泗護大將軍印。

translations.literal: The emperor summoned Zhongqi back to the capital and ordered Guangsi to guard the Grand General's seal.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor recalled Zhongqi to the capital and left Guangsi in charge of the commander's seal.

sentences.zh: 廣泗疏言：「穆壘地處兩山間，築城其中，形如釜底，非屯兵進取之地。

translations.literal: Guangsi memorialized: "Mulei lies between two mountains; building a city within it, the shape is like the bottom of a cauldron—it is not a place to station troops for advance and seizure.
translations.idiomatic: Guangsi reported: "Mulei lies between two mountain ranges. Building a fortress there traps the army in a cauldron-bottom—hardly ground for an offensive camp.

sentences.zh: 今築城未竟，臣與副將軍常賚兩營當要衝，兵止二三百，即鍾琪營亦僅數百，遇警何以抵禦？

translations.literal: Now the city building is not finished; your servant and Deputy General Chang Zhai have two camps at strategic points with only two or three hundred troops, and even Zhongqi's camp has only several hundred—on meeting an alarm, how can we resist?
translations.idiomatic: The fort is unfinished. My camp and Deputy Commander Chang Zhai's hold the passes with only two or three hundred men each, and even Zhongqi's camp has only a few hundred. How are we to meet an attack?

sentences.zh: 準噶爾專用馬，我兵必馬步兼用，而鍾琪立意用車，沙磧殊非所宜。

translations.literal: The Zungars rely exclusively on horses; our army must use horse and foot together, yet Zhongqi is determined to use carts, which are especially unsuited to sandy wastes.
translations.idiomatic: The Zungars fight mounted; our force must combine cavalry and infantry. Yet Zhongqi insists on wagons, which are useless in the desert sands.

sentences.zh: 至馬步兵弓箭、鳥槍之外，止攜木梃，全無刀戟，官兵莫不竊議。

translations.literal: As for horse and foot troops, besides bows, arrows, and muskets they carry only wooden clubs, entirely without knives and halberds; officers and soldiers all whisper in private discussion.
translations.idiomatic: Beyond bows and muskets, the men carry only wooden clubs, with no blades or polearms at all. Officers and soldiers alike murmur against it.

sentences.zh: 穆壘又無牧地，鍾琪留馬二千餘，悉就牧烏蘭烏蘇、科舍圖兩地，敵人窺伺可虞。

translations.literal: Mulei also has no pasture land; Zhongqi left more than two thousand horses, all sent to pasture at Wulan Wusu and Keshetu, where enemy spying is to be feared.
translations.idiomatic: Mulei has no pasture. Zhongqi left more than two thousand horses grazing at Wulan Wusu and Keshetu, inviting enemy reconnaissance.

sentences.zh: 駐兵數万人，糧運最要。

translations.literal: With tens of thousands of troops stationed, grain transport is most important.
translations.idiomatic: With tens of thousands of troops in the field, grain transport is critical.

sentences.zh: 地多叢山大嶺，車駝分運，必繞出沙磧。

translations.literal: The land has many clustered mountains and great ridges; carts and camels transport separately and must detour out of the sandy wastes.
translations.idiomatic: The country is rugged, and wagon and camel convoys must skirt the desert by long detours.

sentences.zh: 鍾琪聞寇至，輒令停運，以此遲緩。

translations.literal: When Zhongqi heard bandits had come, he then ordered transport halted, thereby causing delay.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Zhongqi heard the enemy was near, he halted convoys, and supplies fell behind.

sentences.zh: 鍾琪張皇剛愎，號令不明。

translations.literal: Zhongqi was alarmist, stubborn, and self-willed; his orders were unclear.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongqi is alarmist and obstinate, and his orders are unclear.

sentences.zh: 題奏奉到諭旨，臨時宣傳，莫測誠偽。」

translations.literal: When memorials received imperial edicts, he announced them on the spot, and no one could measure their truth or falsehood."
translations.idiomatic: When edicts arrived he announced them orally on the spot, so no one could tell whether they were genuine."

sentences.zh: 上奪鍾琪官，命廣泗還軍巴爾庫爾。

translations.literal: The emperor stripped Zhongqi of his office and ordered Guangsi to return the army to Barkol.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor stripped Zhongqi of rank and ordered Guangsi to withdraw to Barkol.

sentences.zh: 廣泗奏軍還巴爾庫爾，分兵防洮賚、無克克嶺，斷敵南走道，防廋集察罕、哈馬爾，斷敵西來道；

translations.literal: Guangsi memorialized that the army returned to Barkol, divided troops to guard Zhaolai and Wukekeling and cut off the enemy's southern escape route, and guarded Shoujichahan and Hamar to cut off the enemy's western approach;
translations.idiomatic: Guangsi reported that on returning to Barkol he posted detachments at Zhaolai and Wukekeling to block the enemy's southern retreat, and at Shoujichahan and Hamar to block their approach from the west;

sentences.zh: 巴爾庫爾北為鏡兒泉、噶順、烏卜圖克勒克諸地，東北為圖古里克、特爾庫勒諸地，敵自沙磧來，處處可通，皆置兵守。

translations.literal: north of Barkol are Jing'er Spring, Gashun, Wubutukeleke, and other places; northeast are Tugurike, Teerkule, and other places; the enemy coming from the sandy wastes can pass everywhere—these were all garrisoned.
translations.idiomatic: north of Barkol lie Jing'er Spring, Gashun, and Wubutukeleke; to the northeast lie Tugurike and Teerkule. The enemy could cross the desert at many points, and he posted troops at each.

sentences.zh: 他諸要隘並設卡倫，巡護牧廠，哈密、塔勒納沁皆增兵為備。

translations.literal: At other strategic passes karun were also established to patrol and protect pasture lands; Hami and Talenaxin all increased troops as preparation.
translations.idiomatic: He established karun at other passes, patrolled the pastures, and reinforced Hami and Talenaxin.

sentences.zh: 尋以查郎阿為大將軍，授廣泗正紅旗漢軍都統，留軍。

translations.literal: Soon Cha Langa was made Grand General; Guangsi was appointed Commander-in-Chief of the Plain Red Banner Hanjun and remained with the army.
translations.idiomatic: Cha Langa was soon appointed grand general, and Guangsi was made commander of the Plain Red Banner Hanjun while remaining in the field.

sentences.zh: 十一年，廣泗將萬餘人分駐北山。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year Guangsi led more than ten thousand men to garrison separately on North Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year Guangsi stationed more than ten thousand men on the northern heights in separate camps.

sentences.zh: 十二年，诇寇至烏爾圖河，檄副都統班第達什、降調總兵張元佐及提督樊廷逐捕，越噶順至鄂隆吉大坂，擊破之，斬四百餘人，獲三十六人。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year scouts reported bandits had reached the Wurtu River; he dispatched Deputy Commander-in-Chief Ban Didashi, reduced-rank Commander Zhang Yuanzuo, and Brigade Commander Fan Ting to pursue and capture them; crossing Gashun to the Elongji great ridge, they defeated them, beheaded more than four hundred, and captured thirty-six.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year scouts reported the enemy at the Wurtu River. He sent deputy commander Ban Didashi, demoted commander Zhang Yuanzuo, and brigade commander Fan Ting in pursuit. They crossed Gashun to the Elongji pass, routed the force, killed more than four hundred, and took thirty-six prisoners.

sentences.zh: 捷聞，命議敘。

translations.literal: When victory was reported, he was ordered to deliberate on recording merit.
translations.idiomatic: When news of the victory arrived, the court ordered his services recorded for reward.

sentences.zh: 十三年，準噶爾乞和，師還。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year the Dzungars sued for peace and the army returned.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year the Dzungars sued for peace and the army withdrew.

sentences.zh: 授湖廣總督。

translations.literal: He was appointed governor-general of Huguang.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed governor-general of Huguang.

sentences.zh: 自鄂爾泰定苗疆，至是九股苗復為亂。

translations.literal: From the time Ortai pacified the Miao frontier until now the Nine-Stock Miao rebelled again.
translations.idiomatic: Since Ortai had pacified the Miao frontier, the Nine-Stock Miao had risen again.

sentences.zh: 尚書張照偕將軍哈元生、副將軍董芳率兵討之，久無功。

translations.literal: Minister Zhang Zhao together with General Ha Yuansheng and Deputy General Dong Fang led troops to suppress them, but for a long time achieved nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Minister Zhang Zhao, General Ha Yuansheng, and Deputy General Dong Fang campaigned against them for a long time without success.

sentences.zh: 高宗即位，授廣泗經略，赴貴州，將軍以下聽節制。

translations.literal: When the Gaozong emperor succeeded, Guangsi was appointed campaign superintendent, went to Guizhou, and all ranks from general downward were placed under his command.
translations.idiomatic: When Qianlong succeeded, Guangsi was made campaign superintendent and sent to Guizhou, with every officer from general downward under his command.

sentences.zh: 廣泗疏劾照阻撓軍機，徵集兵數万，元生沿途分佈，用以攻剿者不過三千，顧此失彼。

translations.literal: Guangsi memorialized impeaching Zhao for obstructing military affairs; tens of thousands of troops were mobilized, Yuansheng distributed them along the route, but those used for attack numbered no more than three thousand, attending to one place and losing another.
translations.idiomatic: Guangsi impeached Zhao for obstructing operations. Tens of thousands were mobilized, but Yuansheng scattered them along the march and kept fewer than three thousand for actual fighting, so gains in one place were lost in another.

sentences.zh: 芳駐守八弓，僅事招撫。

translations.literal: Fang garrisoned Bagong and did only pacification by inducement.
translations.idiomatic: Fang held Bagong and did nothing but offer inducements.

sentences.zh: 巡撫元展成治賑，條款紛錯，官民並困。

translations.literal: Provincial governor Yuan Zhancheng managed relief, but regulations were tangled and both officials and people were distressed.
translations.idiomatic: Provincial Governor Yuan Zhancheng handled relief, but confused regulations left officials and commoners alike in distress.

sentences.zh: 上為奪照、芳、展成等官，命廣泗兼領貴州巡撫；

translations.literal: The emperor thereupon stripped Zhao, Fang, Zhancheng, and others of office and ordered Guangsi to hold concurrently the Guizhou governorship;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor stripped Zhao, Fang, Zhancheng, and others of rank and ordered Guangsi to serve concurrently as Guizhou governor;

sentences.zh: 罷元生將軍，以提督聽廣泗驅策。

translations.literal: Yuansheng was dismissed as general, and the brigade commander was placed at Guangsi's disposal.
translations.idiomatic: Yuansheng was removed as general, and the brigade commander was placed under Guangsi's orders.

sentences.zh: 十二月，廣泗至凱里，分兵三道進剿：副將長壽出空稗，總兵王無黨出台營，廣泗督兵出清江地曰雞擺尾，刻期並進。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month Guangsi reached Kaili and divided the army into three columns for the advance: brigade general Changshou out from Kongbai, major general Wang Wudang out from Taiying, Guangsi directing troops from the Qingjiang place called Jibaiwei, all to advance on a fixed date.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month Guangsi reached Kaili and divided his force into three columns: Brigade General Changshou from Kongbai, Major General Wang Wudang from Taiying, and Guangsi himself from Jibaiwei on the Qing River, all to advance on a fixed date.

sentences.zh: 破上九股卦丁等寨，毀其巢，餘苗走入牛皮大箐。

translations.literal: They broke the upper Nine-Stock Guading and other stockades, destroyed their nests, and the remaining Miao fled into Niupi Daqing.
translations.idiomatic: They stormed the upper Nine-Stock strongholds, destroyed the rebel bases, and the survivors fled into Niupi Daqing.

sentences.zh: 乾隆元年正月，廣泗令諸軍合圍，獲其渠包利等，斬萬餘級，諸苗悉定。

translations.literal: In the first month of Qianlong 1 Guangsi ordered all armies to close the encirclement, captured their chieftains Baoli and others, cut off more than ten thousand heads, and all the Miao were pacified.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of Qianlong 1 Guangsi closed the ring, captured chieftains including Baoli, killed more than ten thousand, and pacified the Miao completely.

sentences.zh: 授廣泗雲貴總督，兼領巡撫，進三等阿達哈哈番世職。

translations.literal: Guangsi was appointed Yunnan-Guizhou governor-general, also held the governorship, and was advanced to third-class adaha gusa hereditary rank.
translations.idiomatic: Guangsi was made Yunnan-Guizhou governor-general, retained the governorship, and was advanced to third-class adaha gusa hereditary rank.

sentences.zh: 奏定鎮遠、安順、大定、平遠諸營製，增貴州兵額，都計二千九百有奇。

translations.literal: He memorialized to fix the garrison systems of Zhenyuan, Anshun, Dading, and Pingyuan, increased Guizhou troop quotas, totaling a little more than twenty-nine hundred.
translations.idiomatic: He fixed the garrison systems of Zhenyuan, Anshun, Dading, and Pingyuan and raised Guizhou troop strength to slightly more than twenty-nine hundred.

sentences.zh: 三年，復請濬治清水江、都江，增爐鑄錢。

translations.literal: In the third year he again asked to dredge the Qingshui and Dujiang rivers and add mint furnaces for coin.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he again asked to dredge the Qingshui and Dujiang rivers and add mints.

sentences.zh: 皆下部議行。

translations.literal: All were referred to the ministries for deliberation and implementation.
translations.idiomatic: The ministries approved and implemented each proposal.

sentences.zh: 五年，請入覲，會湖廣城步橫嶺等寨紅苗糾粵瑤為亂，命廣泗往勘。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he asked to come to audience; when Red Miao at Chengbu Hengling and other stockades in Huguang incited Yue Yao to rebel, he was ordered to go and investigate.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he sought an audience, but Red Miao at Chengbu Hengling and other stockades in Huguang had stirred up Yue Yao rebels, and he was sent to investigate.

sentences.zh: 九月，授欽差大臣，楚、粵提鎮以下受節制。

translations.literal: In the ninth month he was appointed imperial commissioner; all brigade commanders and major generals of Huguang and Guangdong were placed under his command.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month he was made imperial commissioner with command over all senior officers of Huguang and Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 十一月，亂定。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month the rebellion was settled.
translations.idiomatic: By the eleventh month the rebellion was over.

sentences.zh: 六年正月，至京師，乞歸葬，賜其父母祭。

translations.literal: In the first month of the sixth year he reached the capital, asked leave to return home for burial, and was granted sacrifices for his parents.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the sixth year he reached the capital, asked leave to bury his parents at home, and was granted funeral sacrifices for them.

sentences.zh: 貴州黎平黑苗复糾粵瑤為亂，命廣泗還貴州按治，獲苗酋石金元等置之法。

translations.literal: Black Miao at Liping in Guizhou again incited Yue Yao to rebel; Guangsi was ordered back to Guizhou to handle the case, captured Miao chieftains Shi Jinyuan and others, and punished them by law.
translations.idiomatic: Black Miao at Liping in Guizhou stirred up Yue Yao rebels again. Guangsi was sent back to Guizhou, captured chieftains including Shi Jinyuan, and punished them under law.

sentences.zh: 十年，加太子少保。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he was given the added title Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year he received the title Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 十一年，大金川土司莎羅奔為亂，調川陝總督。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year the Greater Jinchuan chieftain Suoluo Ben rebelled; Guangsi was transferred to Sichuan-Shaanxi governor-general.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year the Greater Jinchuan chieftain Suoluo Ben rebelled, and Guangsi was transferred to the Sichuan-Shaanxi governor-generalship.

sentences.zh: 廣泗至軍，小金川土司澤旺土舍良爾吉來降。

translations.literal: When Guangsi reached the army, the Lesser Jinchuan chieftain Zewang's tusi Liangerji came to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: When Guangsi reached the front, Liangerji, a tusi under the Lesser Jinchuan chieftain Zewang, surrendered.

sentences.zh: 八月，遣總兵宋宗璋、許應虎分道攻勒烏圍，副將馬良柱攻噶拉依，副將張興、參將買國良繼進。

translations.literal: In the eighth month he dispatched major generals Song Zongzhang and Xu Yinghu to attack Lewuwei by separate routes, brigade general Ma Liangzhu to attack Galayi, and brigade general Zhang Xing and regimental colonel Mai Guoliang to follow up.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month he sent Major Generals Song Zongzhang and Xu Yinghu against Lewuwei on separate axes, Brigade General Ma Liangzhu against Galayi, and Brigade General Zhang Xing and Regimental Colonel Mai Guoliang in support.

sentences.zh: 山險碉堅，轉戰逾二年，師無功。

translations.literal: The mountains were perilous and the blockhouses strong; fighting dragged on for more than two years without success.
translations.idiomatic: The mountains were steep and the blockhouses stubborn; after more than two years of fighting the army had achieved nothing.

sentences.zh: 十三年，疏劾良柱自丹噶撤軍失砲械，命逮詣京師。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year he memorialized impeaching Liangzhu for withdrawing from Dangga and losing cannon and equipment; he was ordered arrested and brought to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year he impeached Liangzhu for withdrawing from Dangga and losing artillery. Liangzhu was ordered arrested and brought to the capital.

sentences.zh: 上授大學士訥親經略，出視師，並起岳鍾琪赴軍，詔責廣泗師老氣怯，調度失機宜。

translations.literal: The emperor appointed Grand Secretary Neqin campaign superintendent to go out and inspect the army, and also recalled Yue Zhongqi to the campaign; an edict reproached Guangsi for an army grown old and timid and for losing opportunities in deployment.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor appointed Grand Secretary Neqin superintendent of the campaign and recalled Yue Zhongqi to the front. An edict rebuked Guangsi for letting the army grow stale and timid and for mishandling opportunities.

sentences.zh: 廣泗奏報攻克戎布寨五十餘碉，諭曰：「此亦小小攻克耳。

translations.literal: Guangsi memorialized reporting the capture of more than fifty blockhouses at Rongbu Stockade; the emperor instructed: "This too is only a small capture.
translations.idiomatic: Guangsi reported the capture of more than fifty blockhouses at Rongbu Stockade. The emperor replied, "That is only a minor gain.

sentences.zh: 佇待捷音，以慰西顧。」

translations.literal: I await news of victory to ease my concern for the west."
translations.idiomatic: I am waiting for real victory to ease my concern for the western frontier."

sentences.zh: 訥親初至，督攻碉，師敗績。

translations.literal: When Neqin first arrived he directed attacks on blockhouses and the army was defeated.
translations.idiomatic: When Neqin arrived he pressed assaults on the blockhouses and was defeated.

sentences.zh: 總兵任舉為驍將，戰沒。

translations.literal: Major general Ren Ju, a fierce fighter, died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: Major General Ren Ju, one of the army's boldest fighters, was killed in action.

sentences.zh: 乃議令官軍築碉，謂與賊共險。

translations.literal: They then deliberated ordering government troops to build blockhouses, saying this would share difficult ground with the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: They then proposed building blockhouses of their own, arguing that this would let them share the enemy's strong points.

sentences.zh: 上以為非策，責廣泗附和推諉，嚴諭詰難。

translations.literal: The emperor held this no strategy and reproached Guangsi for echoing and shirking responsibility, issuing stern instructions of censure.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor rejected the plan and sharply rebuked Guangsi for echoing others and shirking responsibility.

sentences.zh: 訥親劾廣泗分十道進兵，兵力微弱，老師糜餉；

translations.literal: Neqin impeached Guangsi for dividing advance into ten routes with feeble strength, the army grown old and wasting supplies;
translations.idiomatic: Neqin impeached Guangsi for splitting the advance into ten weak columns, keeping the army idle, and wasting supplies;

sentences.zh: 鍾琪亦劾廣泗玩兵養寇，信用良爾吉及漢奸王秋，洩軍事於敵。

translations.literal: Zhongqi also impeached Guangsi for trifling with the army and nurturing the enemy, trusting Liangerji and the Han traitor Wang Qiu and leaking military affairs to the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongqi also charged Guangsi with coddling the enemy, trusting Liangerji and the Han collaborator Wang Qiu, and leaking military intelligence.

sentences.zh: 上責廣泗貽誤軍機，奪官，逮至京師，上御瀛台親鞫。

translations.literal: The emperor reproached Guangsi for jeopardizing military affairs, stripped him of office, had him arrested and brought to the capital, and personally tried him at the Yingtai.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor blamed Guangsi for jeopardizing military operations, stripped him of rank, and had him brought to the capital, where the emperor personally tried him at the Yingtai.

sentences.zh: 廣泗極言其枉，命用刑，辨不已。

translations.literal: Guangsi vehemently declared himself wronged; torture was ordered, yet he argued without cease.
translations.idiomatic: Guangsi insisted he had been wronged. Torture was ordered, but he kept protesting.

sentences.zh: 上諭曰：「金川用兵，張廣泗、訥親前後貽誤。

translations.literal: The emperor instructed: "In the Jinchuan campaign, Zhang Guangsi and Neqin successively brought disaster.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "In the Jinchuan war, Zhang Guangsi and Neqin failed the court one after another.

sentences.zh: 廣泗初至軍，妄為大言，既久無成效，則諉過於部將。

translations.literal: When Guangsi first reached the army he spoke grand empty words; after long lack of results he shifted blame onto subordinate generals.
translations.idiomatic: When Guangsi first arrived he boasted extravagantly; when nothing came of it he blamed his subordinates.

sentences.zh: 及訥親往，乃復觀望推諉，見訥親種種失宜，無一語相告。

translations.literal: When Neqin went out he again looked on and shirked; seeing Neqin's many improprieties, he did not offer a single word of counsel.
translations.idiomatic: When Neqin took command he again held back and shifted blame. He saw Neqin's many mistakes and never offered a word of warning.

sentences.zh: 見其必敗，訕笑非議，備極險忮。

translations.literal: Seeing he was certain to fail, he sneered and criticized, showing the utmost malice.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing defeat coming, he mocked and criticized with the utmost malice.

sentences.zh: 蓋恐此時奏聞，猶或譴責，不若坐視決裂為得計也。

translations.literal: He feared that if he reported now he might still be censured, and thought it a better plan to sit and watch matters rupture.
translations.idiomatic: He feared that reporting now might still bring punishment, and judged it safer to watch the disaster unfold.

sentences.zh: 朕詳悉推勘，如見肺肝。

translations.literal: I have examined this in full detail, as if seeing liver and lungs laid bare.
translations.idiomatic: I have examined this in full, as if I could see his heart and lungs laid bare.

sentences.zh: 訥親且在其術中而不覺矣。

translations.literal: Neqin was even within his schemes without realizing it.
translations.idiomatic: Even Neqin was caught in his schemes without realizing it.

sentences.zh: 廣泗熟嫻軍旅，與訥親並為練達政事之大臣，乃自逞其私，罔卹國事。

translations.literal: Guangsi was well versed in military affairs and, like Neqin, was a minister skilled in government, yet he indulged private ends and disregarded state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Guangsi knew warfare well, and like Neqin he was an experienced statesman, yet both indulged private ends and neglected the state.

sentences.zh: 今朕明正其罪，以彰國憲。」

translations.literal: Now I make their crimes clear to manifest the law of the state."
translations.idiomatic: Now I shall make their crimes clear and uphold the law of the state."

sentences.zh: 下軍機大臣會刑部議罪，當失誤軍機律斬。

translations.literal: The matter was referred to the Grand Council and Ministry of Punishments to deliberate guilt; under the statute for jeopardizing military affairs they were sentenced to execution.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Council and Ministry of Punishments deliberated and sentenced him to death for jeopardizing military operations.

sentences.zh: 十二月，斬廣泗。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month Guangsi was beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month Guangsi was executed.

sentences.zh: 後十日，諭並誅訥親。

translations.literal: Ten days later an edict ordered Neqin executed as well.
translations.idiomatic: Ten days later Neqin was executed as well.

sentences.zh: 論曰：為三軍擇將，豈易言哉？

translations.literal: The commentator says: To choose generals for the three armies—is that easily spoken of?
translations.idiomatic: The historian remarks: Choosing commanders for the armies is no easy matter.

sentences.zh: 查郎阿臨邊未遇敵，按殺成斌、勷。

translations.literal: Cha Lang'a on the frontier did not meet the enemy, yet executed Chengbin and Qing by due process.
translations.idiomatic: Cha Lang'a never met the enemy on the frontier, yet had Chengbin and Qing executed under due process.

sentences.zh: 世謂與查廩有連為修怨，甚矣其枉也！

translations.literal: The world says that because he was connected with Cha Lin he nursed a grudge—how greatly he was wronged!
translations.idiomatic: Later opinion held that he acted from a grudge tied to Cha Lin—a grave injustice!

sentences.zh: 傅爾丹中敵間，師徒撓敗，世宗特寬之；

translations.literal: Fu Erdan fell into the enemy's stratagem and army and master were thrown into defeat; the Shizong emperor specially pardoned him;
translations.idiomatic: Fu Erdan fell for an enemy ruse and his army was shattered, yet the Yongzheng emperor spared him;

sentences.zh: 高宗時復起，至與岳鍾琪同視，何其幸歟！

translations.literal: under the Gaozong emperor he was raised again, even serving with Yue Zhongqi in the same campaign—how fortunate he was!
translations.idiomatic: under Qianlong he was restored and even served again with Yue Zhongqi—what remarkable fortune!

sentences.zh: 若馬爾賽之畏縮，慶復之欺誑，譴當其罪。

translations.literal: As for Ma Ersai's timidity and Qing Fu's deception, their punishments matched their crimes.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Ersai's timidity and Qing Fu's deceit deserved the punishments they received.

sentences.zh: 廣泗傾鍾琪，劾照，知訥親不可撼，乃坐視其敗，以忮殺其身，雖有勞不能逭。

translations.literal: Guangsi undermined Zhongqi and impeached Zhao; knowing Neqin could not be shaken, he sat and watched his defeat, and through malice brought death on himself—though he had merit he could not escape.
translations.idiomatic: Guangsi undermined Zhongqi and impeached Zhao; seeing that Neqin could not be moved, he watched his defeat and was destroyed by his own malice. Merit could not save him.

sentences.zh: 籲，可畏哉！

translations.literal: Alas, how dreadful!
translations.idiomatic: Alas—how dreadful a lesson!
